title: Patient Accounting Standard: Extra Payments, Payoff and Reductions of Enrolled Charges under the Patient Payment Plans
content:
This standard governs how a plan under the Patient Payment Plans treats payments above the installment, payoff, and reductions of enrolled charges made outside the plan.

**1. Paying ahead and paying off.** A patient may pay more than the installment, or pay the plan off, at any time with no penalty. A payoff statement is issued within the tier's payoff-statement period in business days on request.

**2. Applying a prepayment.** A prepayment is applied according to the tier's prepayment method: shortening the term keeps the installment and ends the plan sooner; reducing the installment keeps the end date and lowers the installment.

**3. Reductions outside the plan.** When an enrolled charge is reduced outside the plan (a late insurance payment, a hardship adjustment, a billing correction), the plan balance is reduced by the same amount on the same date and absorbed according to the tier's balance-reduction method.

**4. One reduction per reason.** An enrolled charge is reduced at most once per reason. The judgement rests on the system record of the plan's reductions for that charge, matched by the charge reduced.

**5. Payoff.** When the remaining balance reaches 0.00 the plan is paid off. A payment beyond the remaining balance is applied to the financial account, where it becomes a credit if nothing else is owed.

### Reduction reasons

| Reason for the reduction of an enrolled charge | May be recorded for a charge that already shows a reduction for the same reason |
|---|---|
| Insurance payment | No |
| Hardship adjustment | No |
| Billing correction | No |

A charge that already shows a reduction for one reason may still be reduced once for a different reason.

### Illustration (hypothetical)

A plan's remaining balance stands at 120.00 and the patient pays 150.00. The plan balance reaches 0.00 and the plan is paid off; the 30.00 beyond the remaining balance is applied to the financial account, and becomes a credit if nothing else is owed there.
